## 4. What makes us different — the four pillars (re-validated)

**Plan versus actual, on every task.** The idea the whole data model is built around: every task carries a planned window and an actual one, dates are YYYY-MM-DD local strings, and the difference is rendered everywhere as overdue, done-early and done-late. Judge the app on whether that comparison is visible, truthful and editable wherever work is looked at. _Features: plan.startDate / plan.endDate and actual.startDate / actual.endDate on every task, Overdue, done-early and done-late indicators on cards, in the editor and on the timeline, Draggable, resizable plan bars with SVG dependency arrows, grouped by project, Calendar month grid where a drop shifts plan.endDate and preserves duration, Dashboard RAG health comparing percentage done against percentage of schedule elapsed, Automatic actual-date stamping on status transitions._

**Effort recorded where the work happens.** A per-day activity log with hours, completion status, bottleneck remarks and attachments, with denormalised counters on the task kept correct through batched increments. Judge the app on whether recording an hour is faster than avoiding it, and whether the numbers that come out are ones a manager can defend. _Features: Per-day activity entries with comment, hoursSpent, completion status, bottlenecks and attachments, activityCount, totalHoursLogged, attachmentCount and lastActivityAt kept in sync in the same batch, Single-track timer with a topbar widget and one-click log on stop, Weekly timesheet per person with a project split, exportable as a two-sheet workbook, Workload grid of people by week, drag to rebalance, Bulk edit, delete and export over the activity log, plus a four-step spreadsheet import._

**One AI door, and honesty about what came through it.** Every generative feature goes through askAI / askAIJson; only bridge/ai.mjs spawns the CLI, hermetically, on 127.0.0.1; a company key never reaches a browser; and any fallback is returned and rendered as degraded with a reason. Judge the app on whether it ever passes off a fallback, a mock or a failed grounding as a clean answer. _Features: askAI / askAIJson as the single chokepoint, with claude-code, bridge-api, proxy, api and mock providers, Hermetic CLI invocation with --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --tools "", and a denied tool treated as a failure, NotebookLM grounding that prepends cited material and degrades rather than swallowing a failed lookup, Company keys held server-side behind the aiProxy function, never shipped to a browser, Provider-aware wording so an API-billed bridge never advertises a subscription, Task drafting, quick-add parsing, suggestions, digests and status-report narrative, all through the same door._

**A shared workspace with rules as the enforcement point.** Projects, tasks, activities, templates and comments all belong to exactly one workspace; roles are owner / admin / editor / viewer enforced in firestore.rules, not in the UI; invites are by email with no backend; deletes are soft; and the one world-readable document is a snapshot, never a window. Judge the app on whether the boundary holds when the UI is bypassed. _Features: Workspace isolation across every collection, enforced in firestore.rules and covered by emulator tests, Invite by email with self-claim at sign-in, no UID ever changing hands, Per-project ACLs layered inside the workspace, with storage rules reading the workspace document, Soft delete everywhere plus a Trash view with restore, and hard delete only where no activity references it, Read-only client share links that carry a written-down snapshot, expiring and revocable in the rules, Google sign-in that links an anonymous account and keeps its data._

## 5. Findings

53 findings. IDs: IMP = improvement, BUG = error, MISS = missing feature, POL = polish, NEW = world-class addition. Every finding names files, the page / window / modal / panel where a tester sees it, priority (P0/P1/P2), estimate (S/M/L), target release, and the risk of applying the fix with a Proceed / On-Hold recommendation.

## 6. World-class additions

| # | Addition | Borrowed / adapted from | Why it matters here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Inline editing in the task table | Monday.com · Airtable · ClickUp | The task table already knows every column and its type; making cells editable turns the report into the fastest way to fill in the plan-vs-actual dates this app is built around. |
| 2 | Keyboard-first task actions | Linear | One owner running a whole portfolio is measured by the gap between deciding and recording; a/s/d/p shortcuts close it, and the board already registers a KeyboardSensor. |
| 3 | Estimates versus actual hours | ClickUp · Asana · Monday.com | The app does plan-vs-actual on dates and tracks real hours obsessively, but has nothing to compare those hours to — and the workload grid currently assumes a flat four hours a task. |
| 4 | Per-project custom statuses | Monday.com · ClickUp | Projects already carry phases and custom fields, so a per-project stage vocabulary fits the existing shape; three hardcoded columns force every kind of work into one mould. |
| 5 | WIP limits and column ageing | Kanban practice · Linear · Jira | The board's column counts and the Dashboard's days-in-Doing number already exist; surfacing them as a limit is the cheapest fix for the half-done-everything pattern the blocker panel keeps reporting. |
| 6 | Critical path and slack on the Gantt | Microsoft Project · Monday.com · Smartsheet | Dependency arrows are already drawn; without a critical path they are decoration rather than an answer to which delay actually matters. |
| 7 | Duplicate a task, project or process | Asana · ClickUp · Notion | Templates cover the planned case; duplicate covers the far commoner decided-afterwards case, and the payload-stripping functions it needs are already written. |
| 8 | My Week across every workspace | Motion · Asana My Tasks | The stated user runs several workspaces; today the My-tasks chip filters one board, and the cross-workspace hooks the feature needs already exist for Goals. |
| 9 | Scheduled digest automation | Asana rules · Monday automations | The digest content is already computed for Ask AI and the status report, and the inbox already renders notices — only a time trigger is missing. |
| 10 | Threaded, resolvable comments | Linear · Notion · Asana | The mention and inbox machinery is built and tested; without threads a well-used task becomes twenty equal-weight notes with no conclusion. |
| 11 | Cycles with a burndown | Linear cycles | The app measures hours and lateness but has no bounded period to judge completion against, and completed-date data for the burndown is already stored. |
| 12 | Project-scoped Ask AI with citations | Notion AI · ClickUp Brain | Projects already carry their own notebook id and askAI already grounds with citations; the question people have is project-shaped and asked while looking at the project. |
| 13 | Subtasks that keep their parent when promoted | Asana · ClickUp | Promote currently severs the hierarchy; the typed links array is already the right shape to keep it. |
| 14 | Portfolio view across workspaces | Asana Portfolios · Monday dashboards | The Dashboard's RAG health table is the best thing in the app and can only see one workspace at a time. |
| 15 | Visible offline queue | Linear | The topbar already promises that offline changes will sync but shows no evidence, which makes working on the move feel unsafe. |
| 16 | Installable app with an offline shell | Linear · Notion mobile | A service worker and a mobile layout already exist; a manifest and a cached shell turn a browser tab into something usable on a site visit. |
| 17 | Saved views shared with the workspace | Asana · Linear · Monday.com | A saved table view is the unit of team alignment, and today it is private to whoever built it. |
